source.edition: Elementary Topology, Michael C. Gemignani, Second Edition
source.visualReview: Full supplied PDF pages 77 and 82 inspected at 762×1262, with surrounding supplied prose on PDF pages 76 and 81. Every reconstructed figure was reviewed beside an inspected source crop. Missing printed page 75 was not reconstructed.
source.boundsConvention: sourceBounds is normalized [x,y,width,height] against the full source page. Visually inspected pixel rectangles include graphics and labels and exclude prose and captions.

implementation.semantics: Shape-free immutable Substance snapshots declare maps, membership, inverse correspondences and quotient constructions. Reusable synchronous TSX styles assemble native Penrose geometry.
implementation.graphics: Native Penrose circles, ellipses, lines, polygon, equations and groups; no source raster wrappers.
implementation.appearance: Shared 18px serif mathematical label policy, black outlines and markers, subdued orange and gray hatching for equivalence-class highlights.

verification.exampleLeafTypecheckAndEmit: passed for both projection and endpoint-identification leaf modules
verification.visualReview: All three SVGs optimized and rendered, rasterized on white backgrounds and inspected side by side with source crops. Label sizes adjusted to the shared topology policy after comparison.
verification.scope: Analytic correspondence invariants, equivalence-class membership and actual SVG lowering are checked. Finite numeric tests do not constitute formal proofs or pixel-level equivalence.

figures.sourceContext: Visible central projection diagram with labels P, x, j_P(x), Segment 1 and Segment 2. Example 12 is on absent printed page 75; supplied Example 13 on printed page 76 refers back to it.
geometry: Two closed segments meet at their left endpoint. One rises toward the right; the other descends slightly toward the right.
A ray from P passes through Segment 1's right endpoint to Segment 2's right endpoint. A second ray is vertical through x and j_P(x).
There is no extra edge from P to the segments' shared left endpoint.
Default mathematical coordinates P=(0,2), A=(-0.85,0.08), B=(2.45,-0.2), C=P+0.265(B−P); the marked x is selected on A–C with x-coordinate zero. Its image is computed by ray–segment intersection.
facts: LinearSegment objects store mathematical endpoints; CentralProjection stores P.
CentralProjectionBetween and MapBetween declare the construction, ProjectionCenter binds P, Member and MapsTo bind x and j_P(x).
TopologyOn, ContinuousMap and Homeomorphism describe this independently valid realization.
checks: The chosen analytic projection carries both segment endpoints bijectively.
101 parameter samples have ordered images, ray collinearity and inverse round trips.
A degenerate projection from P itself is rejected.
Actual SVG contains the four source lines and three marked points.
limits: The original Example 12's exact hypotheses and proof are unavailable in the supplied scan. The source graphic is recreated and the chosen realization is independently checked; absent prose is not attributed to the book.
Coordinates approximate the scanned construction. The source's line and print noise are replaced with clean vectors.

figures.sourceContext: Example 13 positions a circle center strictly inside a triangle and gives a radial homeomorphism. The prose says circle onto triangle, while the drawn x lies on the triangle and j(x) on the circle.
geometry: Unfilled circle and triangular boundary share a center C strictly inside the triangle.
The single ray C–j(x) crosses x on the triangle's right edge and ends at j(x) on the circle.
Default center C=(0,0), circle radius 1.16, triangle vertices (−1.58,−0.82), (1.16,−0.6), (0.35,1.43). The marked x is the midpoint of the right edge.
facts: TriangleBoundary and CircleBoundary represent the outlines, rather than filled disks.
RadialProjectionBetween(j,triangle,circle) and MapsTo(j,x,j(x)) preserve the source's marker direction.
InverseMaps(j,j⁻¹), inverse MapBetween and MapsTo facts also represent the prose's circle-to-triangle direction.
Both directions have ContinuousMap and Homeomorphism relations.
checks: Radial circle and triangle helpers are inverse around 80 sampled directions and all triangle vertices.
Every computed circle image has the stated radius.
Centers outside the triangle and zero-length radial directions are rejected.
Actual SVG contains one circle outline, one triangular boundary, one radial ray and three marked points.
limits: The source's prose and displayed marker direction differ. The graphic preserves x and j(x) exactly; the DSL records both inverse homeomorphisms rather than silently swapping the labels.
The original triangle and circular trace are hand drawn; smooth analytic boundaries approximate their geometry.

figures.sourceContext: Definition 5 on supplied printed page 80 defines the identification map and quotient topology. Example 14 on printed page 81 takes [0,1] with its usual topology, identifies 0 with 1 and keeps every interior point equivalent only to itself, producing a circle.
geometry: Upper panel: closed interval 0–x–1 with both endpoints highlighted by hatch marks.
Lower panel: circular quotient with one highlighted top point labeled {0,1} and a bottom point labeled {x}.
The source's two stacked panels are retained with no added arrow or caption inside the SVG.
The circle parameterization t↦(cos(π/2+2π(t−a)/(b−a)),sin(π/2+2π(t−a)/(b−a))) sends both endpoints exactly to the top; default interior representative t=1/2 goes to the bottom.
facts: EndpointIdentification records the entire rule x~y iff x=y or both are endpoints, rather than treating the two drawn classes as the whole quotient.
EquivalenceOn, EquivalentUnder, QuotientOf, ClassOf, ClassInQuotient and Member describe the identification construction.
EquivalenceClass is both a Set of original points and a Point of the QuotientSpace.
IdentificationMap(q,I,Q,R) and IdentificationTopology declare the quotient topology; CircleParameterizes and FactorsThrough express the circle realization through the quotient.
checks: The endpoint relation is reflexive, symmetric and transitive on representative samples; interior classes remain singleton.
Both endpoint circle images are exactly equal, the midpoint maps to the bottom, and sampled distinct interior points have distinct images.
The default two represented classes have no drawing coordinates and participate in both set membership and map images.
Actual SVG retains both panels, three class highlights and the circle boundary.
limits: Only two representative quotient classes are drawn; the full equivalence relation and quotient are declared mathematically.
Ellipse sizes and orange hatching are style-owned visual highlights for single quotient points and are not additional members or neighborhoods.
The source's irregular endpoint parentheses and hatch strokes are approximated by elliptic highlights and analytic hatch chords.
